## Why This Is Asked
Tests binding of feature flags to artifact provenance and touches CI, runtime, and security controls across tenants.

## Key Concepts
- cosign signing and repo public keys
- SBOMs (CycloneDX)
- central provenance store and attestations
- manifest digest binding to provenance
- Kyverno admission policy

## Code Example
```yaml
name: Sign-and-attest
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build -t my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA .
      - name: cosign sign
        run: cosign sign --key cosign.pub my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA
      - name: generate SBOM
        run: cyclonedx-bom -o bom.xml my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA
      - name: upload SBOM
        run: curl -X POST -F file=@bom.xml https://provenance-store.local/upload
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test cross-tenant consistency?
- How would you rotate keys without breaking in-flight deploys?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests designing end-to-end security controls across CI and runtime in a multi-cloud Kubernetes environment, combining image signing, registry governance, and host attestation. 

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore/cosign image signing and Rekor attestations
- OPA/Gatekeeper policy constraints for manifests
- Digest pinning and registry allowlists
- TPM/attestation-based runtime scheduling
- End-to-end CI validation and production-time checks

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate for image signature
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: K8sImageSig
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageSig
        listKind: K8sImageSigList
        plural: k8simagesigs
        singular: k8simagesig
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8simagesig
        violation["image unsigned"] {
          input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
          image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
          not image.endswith("@sha256:")
        }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test revocation of a signed image in CI and runtime?
- How would you handle edge cases like multi- tenant imaging workflows or private registries?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in multi-cloud tenancy, data residency compliance, and automated policy enforcement. It requires understanding of cross-cloud networking, secret management patterns, service mesh security, and continuous verification using Prometheus. Candidates must demonstrate end-to-end enforcement—from namespace isolation through egress traffic, mTLS, and progressive delivery.

## Key Concepts

- **Cross-cloud tenancy isolation**: Enforcing hard boundaries between tenants across AWS, GCP, and Azure requires consistent policy engines that understand region semantics and cloud-specific resource constraints.

- **Admission control patterns**: Kyverno excels at mutation and generation, while OPA Gatekeeper provides robust enforce-or-deny semantics. Using both in concert allows for defense-in-depth.

- **Secret management**: Preventing literal secrets in environment variables and enforcing SecretStore references is critical for security compliance in regulated environments.

- **Network policy enforcement**: Per-tenant egress gateways with namespace-aware NetworkPolicies ensure traffic cannot leak across tenant boundaries.

- **Service mesh integration**: SPIRE provides automated certificate management, but admission policies must ensure workloads are properly registered before receiving traffic.

- **Progressive delivery with SLO gates**: Integrating Prometheus metrics into the deployment pipeline enables data-driven rollout decisions that protect production reliability.

## Why This Is Asked

- Progressive delivery with Argo Rollouts Canary
- AnalysisTemplate and Prometheus metrics
- Promotion rules based on consecutive analyses and SLO breach thresholds
- CI gates validating manifest shape and rollout strategy
- Rollback/promotion semantics in production

## Code Example

```yaml
# AnalysisTemplate (Prometheus-based)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-analysis
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: error-rate
    successCondition: result < 0.01
    failureCondition: result >= 0.05
    provider:
      prometheus:
        address: http://prometheus-operated.default.svc.cluster.local
        query: avg(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

```yaml
# Minimal Rollout using Canary
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myservice
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myservice
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myregistry/myservice:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-analysis
      stepWeight: 20
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (minimal)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
```

## Why This Is Asked
This task tests practical CI gating for container hygiene: linting with Hadolint and enforcing image tagging discipline across manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Hadolint integration in GitHub Actions
- YAML parsing to inspect image tags
- Regular expressions for pinning (no latest, no -dev) and clear failure messages
- Practical debugging of lint vs. policy failures

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-docker-k8s.yml
name: CI Gate: Dockerfile lint + tag pin
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ '**' ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3
        with:
          dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
      - name: Check pinned image tags
        run: |
          set -e
          if grep -RIn 'image:.*:.*(latest|dev.*)' manifests || true; then
            echo 'Unpinned image tag detected' ; exit 1;
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale this gate to many repos?
- How would you extend checks for other tag policies (sha256 digests)?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime, policy-driven security for multi-tenant clusters, including per-tenant exceptions, scalable policy storage, and practical CI validation.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego enforcement
- Runtime security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, hostPath, privileged, SETUID checks
- Central PolicyStore for per-tenant overrides
- CI validation: dry-run, Gatekeeper evaluation, and manifest validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: runtimepolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RuntimePolicy
        listKind: RuntimePolicyList
        plural: runtimepolicies
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package runtimepolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
        msg := "container must run as non-root"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        any_cont := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not any_cont.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "container must have readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      }
      # Additional rules for hostPath, privileged, and SETUID would follow similarly
```

Why This Is Asked
- Tests policy-as-code skills for multi-tenant Kubernetes environments
- Evaluates ability to translate security requirements into enforceable runtime and CI gates

Key Concepts
- Kyverno, Pod Security Standards, Resource limits, CI gates, Drift detection

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deployments
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must define a secure securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drop all capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: "true"
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
  - name: require-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must specify resource limits and requests"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
```

Failing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: insecure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing Test Manifest

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "64Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
          limits:
            memory: "128Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
```

CI Validation Steps
```bash
# Install Kyverno CLI
brew install kyverno

# Validate policies against manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest deployment.yaml

# CI/CD integration example (GitHub Actions)
- name: Validate Kubernetes manifests
  run: |
    kyverno apply policy.yaml -f deploy/
```

Runtime Gate Demonstration
```bash
# Apply the policy cluster-wide
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Verify policy is active
kubectl get clusterpolicy require-secure-deployments

# Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest (will fail)
kubectl apply -f insecure-deployment.yaml
# Error: Validation failed: Each container must define a secure securityContext...

# Deploy compliant manifest (will succeed)
kubectl apply -f secure-deployment.yaml
# deployment.apps/secure-app created
```
